html:
An outbreak of SARS (severe acute respiratory syndrome), a pneumonia caused by a new coronavirus, which began in Guangdong in southern China in late 2002. The virus likely passed from bats to people through animals sold in markets.

Chinese officials played down the first cases. In February 2003 an infected doctor from Guangdong stayed at a hotel in Hong Kong, and guests carried the virus to Vietnam, Singapore and Canada. Hong Kong was hit hardest outside the mainland. The World Health Organization issued a global alert in March 2003. Carlo Urbani, the doctor who first raised the alarm in Hanoi, died of it.

Some 8,000 people fell ill in about 29 countries and nearly 800 died. Quarantine, masks and isolation stopped it by July 2003, and only a few lab-linked cases followed in 2004.

SARS taught East Asia lessons it used against the COVID-19 pandemic that began in China in 2019.
sum: An outbreak of SARS (severe acute respiratory syndrome), a pneumonia caused by a new coronavirus, which began in Guangdong in southern China in late 2002. The virus likely passed from bats to people through animals sold in markets.
